focus: Adversarial deep sweep: ChannelMessageListItem.tsx cross-file interactions, legacy template edge cases, render_template_message subject pipeline, db/schema.rb correctness, spec coverage gaps
methodology: Read the full diff, full spec, all 5 round-1 agent reports, and the qa-run-1 round-2 consolidated findings. Then performed targeted analysis of: (1) ChannelMessageListItem.tsx fix correctness and cross-file interactions with ChannelMessageTemplateModal, (2) legacy template handling in ChannelMessageTemplateSelectionModal and ChannelMessageNew when template subject is nil/empty, (3) render_template_message subject pipeline including Mustache.render of empty subject_source, (4) db/schema.rb column definitions vs migration, (5) full spec re-read hunting for requirements consistently missed by all prior agents.

channelMessageListItem_fix.details: Passing subject: "" is the right choice for the 'Create template from message' flow. The modal's initializer applies `props.channelMessageTemplate.subject || defaultSubject`, so empty string triggers the template-variable default '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}'. This matches the spec's Data flow section: template create modal shows variables literally because no single candidate context applies. Using message.subject (the rendered candidate-specific subject) would be wrong for a template.

legacy_template_edge_cases.details: Traced the full chain: legacy template with nil subject -> render_template_message produces subject_raw: '' -> frontend ChannelMessageTemplateSelectionModal uses `mailMerge?.subjectRaw &&` conditional rendering -> empty string is falsy -> subject preview hidden for legacy templates. In ChannelMessageNew, when a legacy template is inserted, `mailMerge?.subjectRaw` is falsy so setSubject is not called and the field keeps its current rendered default. Both paths degrade gracefully.

schema_vs_migration.details: Migration adds 4 columns: channel_messages.subject (string, null), channel_messages.mailgun_message_id (string, null), channel_message_templates.subject (string, null), jobs.apply_response_template_subject (string, null). Schema dump confirms all 4 at the correct positions in their respective tables. The unrelated AI feature tables in the schema dump are from a separate merged branch and do not interact with the email-subjects feature.

spec_coverage_gap_hunt.details: Re-read every spec requirement with fresh eyes. All backend requirements (migration, validator rename, parse_text rename, HiringStageMessageAutomationJob subject threading, apply-response pipeline, inbound capture, mailer fallback, controller permits/sanitize, serializer exposure, render_template_message extension, anonymization, default template seeds) are implemented. All frontend requirements (yup schemas, 4 subject input surfaces, per-surface default rendering, template selection preview, repopulate-on-error for 2 of 4 surfaces) are implemented. The 2 surfaces missing repopulate-on-error (ChannelMessageTemplateModal and HiringStageAutomationModal inline template) were already captured as C-003 in qa-run-1. No new gaps identified.
